# Metric dictionary

<!-- GENERATED from config/metrics.yaml by `make docs`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Units: `usd` · `frac` (0.15 = 15.0%) · `pp` (percentage points, stored as a fraction) · `x` (multiple) · `days` · `score` · `bool`. Better: ↑ higher · ↓ lower · · neutral.

## Size and liquidity

| id | Name | Definition | Inputs | Unit | Better | Tier | Basis | P | n/m for | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `price` | Price | Last close of the primary ticker (the most liquid common class). On its own date the unadjusted and split-adjusted closes are the same. STALE_DATA if the last bar is more than 7 days before the build's price date.<br>**Tells you:** What one share of the primary listed class last closed at.<br>**Misleads when:** On its own it says nothing about value: a $5 share can be dearer than a $500 one once share count and earnings are counted. | close | usd | · | price | daily | P0 | — | live |
| `market_cap` | Market cap | Unadjusted close × shares outstanding (§4.3 rules 11–12), shares adjusted for splits after the count's share basis, up to the price date: a cover-page count's own date, or for a balance-sheet or diluted count the date its filing was issued (statements already reflect a split made before they're issued). Share basis: the latest cover-page total (else balance-sheet, else diluted weighted count, DERIVED_INPUT); for an Up-C, its economic count (the sum of its cover-page classes). Multi-class companies: Σ class shares × a close per class, counts from the latest 10-K/10-Q cover: each separately listed class at its own close; an unlisted class the filing confirms has the same dividend and liquidation rights (quoted in config/share_classes.yaml `unlisted_economic`) at the close of the listed class it converts into. Voting-only classes never count. STALE_DATA if the share count is more than a year older than the latest balance sheet.<br>**Tells you:** What the market values the whole company's equity at today.<br>**Misleads when:** It ignores debt and cash, so two companies with the same market cap can cost very different amounts to own outright. | close, shares_outstanding | usd | · | price | mixed | P0 | foreign_filers | live |
| `enterprise_value` | Enterprise value | market_cap + total_debt + preferred + minority_interest − cash − st_investments (MRQ balances). Preferred, minority interest and short-term investments not tagged on the balance sheet count as none (noted); total_debt must be tagged. total_debt includes finance leases where the filing presents them outside debt (when no filing says where, they're left out and the ⓘ says so: INPUT_EXCLUDES); operating leases are excluded.<br>**Tells you:** The price of the whole business: equity plus debt and other claims, minus cash.<br>**Misleads when:** Operating leases, pensions, finance leases the filing doesn't place, and other debt-like items are left out, so EV understates the claims on lease-heavy or pension-heavy companies. | market_cap, total_debt, preferred, minority_interest, cash, st_investments | usd | · | price | mixed | P0 | banks, insurance, capital_markets, foreign_filers | live |
| `revenue_ttm` | Revenue (TTM) | Sum of the last 4 discrete quarters (contiguous), or the FY if the latest period is a fiscal year.<br>**Tells you:** How much the company sold over the last twelve months.<br>**Misleads when:** Revenue isn't profit, and it can include pass-through amounts or one-off sales that won't repeat. | revenue | usd | · | sec | ttm | P0 | — | live |
| `avg_dollar_volume_3m` | Avg $ volume (3m) | mean(close × volume) over the last 63 sessions. Null (INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY) with fewer sessions.<br>**Tells you:** How much money changes hands in the stock on a typical day, a rough guide to how easily it can be bought or sold.<br>**Misleads when:** A single heavy day (an index change, news) can lift the average well above what normally trades. | close, volume | usd | ↑ | price | daily | P0 | — | live |

## Valuation

| id | Name | Definition | Inputs | Unit | Better | Tier | Basis | P | n/m for | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pe_ttm` | P/E (TTM) | market_cap / net_income_ttm. Null (NEGATIVE_DENOMINATOR) if NI ≤ 0.<br>**Tells you:** How many years of the last twelve months' profit the share price pays for.<br>**Misleads when:** Earnings include one-off gains and charges, and a cyclical company looks cheapest on P/E exactly when its profits are at a peak. | market_cap, net_income | x | ↓ | price | mixed | P0 | foreign_filers | live |
| `earnings_yield` | Earnings yield | net_income_ttm / market_cap. Keeps negatives, so losses rank last.<br>**Tells you:** Last twelve months' profit as a share of market cap, the inverse of P/E, so losses can still be ranked.<br>**Misleads when:** It uses net income, which carries the same one-off items as P/E, and it ignores debt. | net_income, market_cap | frac | ↑ | price | mixed | P0 | foreign_filers | live |
| `ev_ebit` | EV/EBIT | enterprise_value / ebit_ttm (EBIT = reported operating income). Null (NEGATIVE_DENOMINATOR) if EBIT ≤ 0.<br>**Tells you:** How many years of operating profit the whole business (equity and debt) costs.<br>**Misleads when:** Operating profit can include restructuring charges or gains, and it ignores how much the business must reinvest to keep earning it. | enterprise_value, operating_income | x | ↓ | price | mixed | P0 | banks, insurance, capital_markets, foreign_filers | live |
| `ebit_ev` | EBIT/EV | ebit_ttm / enterprise_value. Null (NEGATIVE_DENOMINATOR) if EV ≤ 0. Keeps negative EBIT.<br>**Tells you:** Operating profit as a share of what the whole business costs, Greenblatt's earnings yield.<br>**Misleads when:** A single good year, or a company whose debt isn't fully tagged, can make it look much cheaper than it is. | operating_income, enterprise_value | frac | ↑ | price | mixed | P0 | banks, insurance, capital_markets, foreign_filers | live |
| `ev_ebitda` | EV/EBITDA | enterprise_value / ebitda_ttm (EBITDA = operating income + D&A). Null (NEGATIVE_DENOMINATOR) if EBITDA ≤ 0.<br>**Tells you:** How many years of operating profit before depreciation the whole business costs.<br>**Misleads when:** EBITDA leaves out depreciation, which is a real cost for capital-heavy businesses, so they can look cheaper than they are. | enterprise_value, ebitda | x | ↓ | price | mixed | P0 | banks, insurance, capital_markets, foreign_filers | live |
| `ev_sales` | EV/Sales | enterprise_value / revenue_ttm.<br>**Tells you:** How much the whole business costs per dollar of yearly revenue.<br>**Misleads when:** It ignores margins: a low EV/Sales is only cheap if sales turn into profit. | enterprise_value, revenue | x | ↓ | price | mixed | P0 | banks, insurance, capital_markets, foreign_filers | live |
| `p_fcf` | P/FCF | market_cap / fcf_ttm (FCF = CFO − capex). Null (NEGATIVE_DENOMINATOR) if FCF ≤ 0.<br>**Tells you:** How many years of free cash flow the share price pays for.<br>**Misleads when:** Free cash flow swings with working capital and the timing of capital spending, so one year can flatter or punish it. | market_cap, fcf | x | ↓ | price | mixed | P1 | foreign_filers | live |
| `fcf_yield` | FCF yield | fcf_ttm / market_cap. Keeps negatives.<br>**Tells you:** Free cash flow as a share of market cap: the cash the business produced for each dollar of equity value.<br>**Misleads when:** It treats stock-based pay as free, and a low-capex year (or a working-capital release) can inflate it. | fcf, market_cap | frac | ↑ | price | mixed | P0 | foreign_filers | live |
| `pb` | P/B | market_cap / equity (MRQ). Null (NEGATIVE_DENOMINATOR) if equity ≤ 0.<br>**Tells you:** How the share price compares with the accounting value of equity on the balance sheet.<br>**Misleads when:** Book value misses brands, software and staff skills, and buybacks shrink it, so asset-light companies always look dear. | market_cap, equity | x | ↓ | price | mixed | P0 | foreign_filers | live |
| `dividend_yield` | Dividend yield | dividends_paid_ttm / market_cap (dividends are a positive outflow in XBRL). Untagged dividends / buybacks / issuance count as none (noted) when the period's cash-flow statement is tagged (CFO present); otherwise MISSING_INPUT.<br>**Tells you:** Dividends paid over the last twelve months as a share of market cap.<br>**Misleads when:** A falling share price raises the yield, so a high yield can be a sign that the market expects a cut. | dividends_paid, market_cap | frac | ↑ | price | mixed | P0 | foreign_filers | live |
| `buyback_yield` | Net buyback yield | (buybacks_ttm − stock_issued_ttm) / market_cap. Untagged dividends / buybacks / issuance count as none (noted) when the period's cash-flow statement is tagged (CFO present); otherwise MISSING_INPUT.<br>**Tells you:** Net money spent buying back shares (after shares issued) over the last twelve months, as a share of market cap.<br>**Misleads when:** It measures cash spent, not shares retired, so buybacks that only offset stock-based pay can still look generous. | buybacks, stock_issued, market_cap | frac | ↑ | price | mixed | P0 | foreign_filers | live |
| `shareholder_yield` | Shareholder yield | dividend_yield + buyback_yield. Excludes debt paydown (unlike Faber's version).<br>**Tells you:** Dividends plus net buybacks as a share of market cap: everything handed back to shareholders in a year.<br>**Misleads when:** It leaves out debt paydown, and payouts funded by new borrowing count the same as payouts funded by cash flow. | dividend_yield, buyback_yield | frac | ↑ | price | mixed | P0 | foreign_filers | live |
| `ncav_to_mcap` | NCAV / market cap | (current_assets − total_liabilities) / market_cap (MRQ balances).<br>**Tells you:** Current assets minus all liabilities, compared with the market cap: Graham's net-net test.<br>**Misleads when:** Inventory and receivables are taken at book value, which may be far more than they would fetch in a sale. | current_assets, total_liabilities, market_cap | frac | ↑ | price | mixed | P0 | foreign_filers | live |

## Profitability and returns

| id | Name | Definition | Inputs | Unit | Better | Tier | Basis | P | n/m for | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gross_margin` | Gross margin | gross_profit_ttm / revenue_ttm. Gross profit is derived as revenue − cost_of_revenue when untagged (DERIVED_INPUT).<br>**Tells you:** The share of revenue left after the direct cost of the goods or services sold.<br>**Misleads when:** Companies draw the line between cost of sales and operating expenses differently, so margins across industries rarely compare. | gross_profit, revenue | frac | ↑ | sec | ttm | P0 | banks, insurance, capital_markets | live |
| `operating_margin` | Operating margin | ebit_ttm / revenue_ttm (EBIT = reported operating income).<br>**Tells you:** The share of revenue left as operating profit, after running costs but before interest and tax.<br>**Misleads when:** One-off charges and gains go through operating profit, so a single year can be unusually high or low. | operating_income, revenue | frac | ↑ | sec | ttm | P0 | — | live |
| `ebitda_margin` | EBITDA margin | ebitda_ttm / revenue_ttm (EBITDA = operating income + D&A from the cash-flow statement).<br>**Tells you:** Operating profit before depreciation and amortisation, as a share of revenue.<br>**Misleads when:** Depreciation is a real cost for asset-heavy businesses, so a high EBITDA margin can hide a low real margin. | ebitda, revenue | frac | ↑ | sec | ttm | P1 | — | live |
| `net_margin` | Net margin | net_income_ttm / revenue_ttm.<br>**Tells you:** The share of revenue left as profit for shareholders, after every cost, interest and tax.<br>**Misleads when:** It includes one-off items, tax credits and gains on investments, so it moves for reasons unrelated to the business. | net_income, revenue | frac | ↑ | sec | ttm | P0 | — | live |
| `fcf_margin` | FCF margin | fcf_ttm / revenue_ttm (FCF = CFO − capex).<br>**Tells you:** The share of revenue that turned into free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capital spending).<br>**Misleads when:** It counts stock-based pay as free and moves with working capital, so one year can look much better than the next. | fcf, revenue | frac | ↑ | sec | ttm | P0 | — | live |
| `roe` | ROE | net_income_ttm / average equity, where average = (MRQ + instant nearest 1 year earlier, ±45 days) / 2. Null (NEGATIVE_DENOMINATOR) if average equity ≤ 0.<br>**Tells you:** Profit as a share of shareholders' equity: how hard the equity on the books is working.<br>**Misleads when:** Debt and buybacks shrink equity and raise ROE without the business improving. | net_income, equity | frac | ↑ | sec | mixed | P0 | — | live |
| `roa` | ROA | net_income_ttm / average total_assets ((MRQ + 1 year earlier) / 2).<br>**Tells you:** Profit as a share of total assets: how much profit the whole balance sheet produces.<br>**Misleads when:** Comparing across industries is unfair: banks and asset-heavy businesses always score low, software companies high. | net_income, total_assets | frac | ↑ | sec | mixed | P0 | — | live |
| `roic` | ROIC | nopat_ttm / average invested capital. NOPAT = EBIT × (1 − t); t = income_tax / pretax_income clamped to [0, 35%]; if pretax income ≤ 0, t = 21% with note ASSUMED_TAX_RATE. Invested capital = total_debt + equity + minority_interest − cash − st_investments, averaged over MRQ and the balance sheet about a year earlier (on the fiscal-year history: that fiscal year end and the one before) (untagged minority interest and short-term investments count as none); null (NEGATIVE_DENOMINATOR) if the average ≤ 0.<br>**Tells you:** After-tax operating profit as a share of the capital invested in the business (debt plus equity, less cash).<br>**Misleads when:** Write-downs and buybacks can shrink invested capital and inflate ROIC, and the tax rate is assumed when pretax income is negative. | operating_income, income_tax, pretax_income, total_debt, equity, minority_interest, cash, st_investments | frac | ↑ | sec | mixed | P0 | banks, insurance, capital_markets | live |
| `greenblatt_roc` | Return on capital (Greenblatt) | ebit_ttm / (net_working_capital + net_ppe), MRQ balances. NWC = (current_assets − cash − st_investments) − (current_liabilities − debt_current); untagged short-term investments and current debt count as none. Null (NEGATIVE_DENOMINATOR) if the denominator ≤ 0.<br>**Tells you:** Operating profit as a share of the working capital and fixed assets the business needs, Greenblatt's return on capital.<br>**Misleads when:** It leaves out goodwill and leased assets, so acquirers and lease-heavy businesses look more capital-light than they are. | operating_income, current_assets, cash, st_investments, current_liabilities, debt_current, ppe_net | frac | ↑ | sec | mixed | P0 | banks, insurance, capital_markets | live |
| `cash_conversion` | Cash conversion | cfo_ttm / net_income_ttm. Null (NEGATIVE_DENOMINATOR) if NI ≤ 0.<br>**Tells you:** How much operating cash flow each dollar of reported profit brought in.<br>**Misleads when:** Working-capital swings move it a lot in a single year, and it's undefined when profit is zero or negative. | cfo, net_income | x | ↑ | sec | ttm | P0 | — | live |
| `sbc_to_revenue` | SBC / revenue | sbc_ttm / revenue_ttm.<br>**Tells you:** Stock-based pay as a share of revenue: a cost that doesn't show up in free cash flow.<br>**Misleads when:** It doesn't show how much the share count actually grew, since buybacks can offset the new shares. | sbc, revenue | frac | ↓ | sec | ttm | P0 | — | live |
| `fcf_after_sbc_margin` | FCF after SBC margin | (fcf_ttm − sbc_ttm) / revenue_ttm.<br>**Tells you:** Free cash flow after treating stock-based pay as a cash cost, as a share of revenue.<br>**Misleads when:** It counts all stock pay at its accounting value, which may differ from what the shares are worth when they vest. | fcf, sbc, revenue | frac | ↑ | sec | ttm | P1 | — | live |

## Growth

| id | Name | Definition | Inputs | Unit | Better | Tier | Basis | P | n/m for | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `revenue_growth_yoy` | Revenue growth (YoY) | revenue_ttm / revenue_ttm_1y_ago − 1. Null (NEGATIVE_DENOMINATOR) if the prior value ≤ 0.<br>**Tells you:** How much revenue grew over the last twelve months compared with the twelve months before.<br>**Misleads when:** Acquisitions, currency moves and a weak year-ago period all lift it without the business itself growing faster. | revenue | frac | ↑ | sec | ttm | P0 | — | live |
| `revenue_cagr_3y` | Revenue CAGR (3y) | (revenue_FY0 / revenue_FY−3)^(1/3) − 1. Null (NEGATIVE_DENOMINATOR) if the start ≤ 0; INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY with fewer than 4 FYs.<br>**Tells you:** Average yearly revenue growth over the last three fiscal years.<br>**Misleads when:** It only looks at the start and end years, so a big acquisition or a bad starting year can dominate. | revenue | frac | ↑ | sec | fy | P0 | — | live |
| `revenue_cagr_5y` | Revenue CAGR (5y) | (revenue_FY0 / revenue_FY−5)^(1/5) − 1. Null if the start ≤ 0 or fewer than 6 FYs.<br>**Tells you:** Average yearly revenue growth over the last five fiscal years.<br>**Misleads when:** It only looks at the start and end years, and five years back the company may have been a different business. | revenue | frac | ↑ | sec | fy | P1 | — | live |
| `eps_growth_yoy` | EPS growth (YoY) | Computed from TTM net income, not reported EPS: (net_income_ttm / diluted shares) ÷ the same a year earlier − 1. Diluted shares = the weighted count for the quarter ending at the TTM end, or the fiscal-year count at a fiscal year end. Preferred dividends are not subtracted. The earlier count is adjusted for splits between the two counts that the company's own filings confirm (a later filing restated a share count by the split's ratio). Null (NEGATIVE_DENOMINATOR) if the prior EPS ≤ 0.<br>**Tells you:** How much profit per share grew over the last twelve months, computed from net income and diluted shares.<br>**Misleads when:** Buybacks raise it even when profit is flat, and one-off items in either year can swing it wildly. | net_income, diluted_shares | frac | ↑ | sec | ttm | P0 | — | live |
| `ebit_growth_yoy` | EBIT growth (YoY) | ebit_ttm / ebit_ttm_1y_ago − 1. Null (NEGATIVE_DENOMINATOR) if the prior value ≤ 0.<br>**Tells you:** How much operating profit grew over the last twelve months compared with the twelve months before.<br>**Misleads when:** Growth from a small or depressed base looks huge, and one-off items in either year distort it. | operating_income | frac | ↑ | sec | ttm | P1 | — | live |
| `fcf_growth_yoy` | FCF growth (YoY) | fcf_ttm / fcf_ttm_1y_ago − 1. Null (NEGATIVE_DENOMINATOR) if the prior value ≤ 0.<br>**Tells you:** How much free cash flow grew over the last twelve months compared with the twelve months before.<br>**Misleads when:** Free cash flow is lumpy, so large swings are common and often reverse the next year. | fcf | frac | ↑ | sec | ttm | P1 | — | live |
| `gross_margin_change_yoy` | Gross margin change | gross_margin − gross_margin_1y_ago (TTM), in percentage points stored as a fraction.<br>**Tells you:** How many percentage points the gross margin moved over the last year.<br>**Misleads when:** A change in product mix or a one-off cost can move it without anything changing in the core business. | gross_margin | pp | ↑ | sec | ttm | P0 | banks, insurance, capital_markets | live |
| `operating_margin_change_yoy` | Operating margin change | operating_margin − operating_margin_1y_ago (TTM), in percentage points stored as a fraction.<br>**Tells you:** How many percentage points the operating margin moved over the last year.<br>**Misleads when:** One-off charges in either year can make a normal year look like a big improvement. | operating_margin | pp | ↑ | sec | ttm | P0 | — | live |
| `share_count_change_yoy` | Share count change | diluted_shares (latest discrete quarter) / same quarter 1 year ago − 1; on the fiscal-year history, the full-year diluted weighted average / the prior fiscal year's − 1. The earlier count is adjusted for splits between the two counts that the company's own filings confirm (a later filing restated a share count by the split's ratio).<br>**Tells you:** How much the diluted share count changed in a year: positive means dilution, negative means buybacks.<br>**Misleads when:** Diluted counts move with the share price (options in or out of the money), an acquisition paid in shares raises it for a reason, and splits the filings don't confirm (ADR ratio changes, a predecessor's comparatives) are not adjusted. | diluted_shares | frac | ↓ | sec | q | P0 | — | live |
| `rule_of_40` | Rule of 40 | revenue_growth_yoy + fcf_margin.<br>**Tells you:** Revenue growth plus FCF margin, a quick balance test of growth against profitability.<br>**Misleads when:** It was made for subscription software, and FCF margin ignores stock-based pay. | revenue_growth_yoy, fcf_margin | frac | ↑ | sec | ttm | P0 | — | live |

## Balance sheet and health

| id | Name | Definition | Inputs | Unit | Better | Tier | Basis | P | n/m for | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `net_debt` | Net debt | total_debt − cash − st_investments (negative = net cash; untagged short-term investments count as none). total_debt includes finance leases where the filing presents them outside debt (when no filing says where, they're left out and the ⓘ says so: INPUT_EXCLUDES); operating leases are excluded.<br>**Tells you:** Debt minus cash and short-term investments; negative means the company holds more cash than debt.<br>**Misleads when:** Operating leases and pensions aren't counted, and cash may be trapped abroad or owed to customers. | total_debt, cash, st_investments | usd | ↓ | sec | mrq | P0 | — | live |
| `net_debt_to_ebitda` | Net debt / EBITDA | net_debt / ebitda_ttm. Null (NEGATIVE_DENOMINATOR) if EBITDA ≤ 0. Finance leases count in debt as for net_debt.<br>**Tells you:** How many years of operating profit before depreciation it would take to pay off net debt.<br>**Misleads when:** EBITDA flatters asset-heavy businesses, and leases and pensions aren't counted as debt. | net_debt, ebitda | x | ↓ | sec | mixed | P0 | banks, insurance, capital_markets, foreign_filers | live |
| `debt_to_equity` | Debt / equity | total_debt / equity. Null (NEGATIVE_DENOMINATOR) if equity ≤ 0. Finance leases count in total_debt as for net_debt.<br>**Tells you:** Total debt compared with shareholders' equity on the balance sheet.<br>**Misleads when:** Buybacks and write-downs shrink equity and make the ratio jump without any new borrowing. | total_debt, equity | x | ↓ | sec | mrq | P0 | — | live |
| `current_ratio` | Current ratio | current_assets / current_liabilities.<br>**Tells you:** Current assets compared with bills due within a year: a rough test of short-term liquidity.<br>**Misleads when:** Slow-moving inventory counts as fully liquid, and some healthy businesses run below 1 on purpose. | current_assets, current_liabilities | x | ↑ | sec | mrq | P0 | banks, insurance, capital_markets | live |
| `quick_ratio` | Quick ratio | (cash + st_investments + receivables) / current_liabilities (untagged short-term investments count as none).<br>**Tells you:** Cash, short-term investments and receivables compared with bills due within a year.<br>**Misleads when:** Receivables may not all be collected, and it says nothing about cash coming in from operations. | cash, st_investments, receivables, current_liabilities | x | ↑ | sec | mrq | P1 | banks, insurance, capital_markets | live |
| `interest_coverage` | Interest coverage | ebit_ttm / interest_expense_ttm. Null (NO_INTEREST_EXPENSE) if interest expense is zero for the TTM, or isn't tagged while total debt is zero; untagged with debt (or unknown debt) is MISSING_INPUT.<br>**Tells you:** How many times operating profit covers the year's interest cost.<br>**Misleads when:** A good year flatters it, and floating-rate debt can make next year's interest bill much higher. | operating_income, interest_expense | x | ↑ | sec | ttm | P0 | banks, insurance, capital_markets | live |
| `altman_z` | Altman Z (1968) | 1.2·WC/TA + 1.4·RE/TA + 3.3·EBIT/TA + 0.6·MktCap/TL + 1.0·Sales/TA, with WC = current_assets − current_liabilities. Balances MRQ, EBIT and sales TTM. n/m for financials and REITs.<br>**Tells you:** A five-part score from balance-sheet and profit ratios, built to separate distressed manufacturers from healthy ones.<br>**Misleads when:** It was built on 1960s US manufacturers and its weights don't suit service, software or financial companies. | current_assets, current_liabilities, total_assets, retained_earnings, operating_income, market_cap, total_liabilities, revenue | score | ↑ | price | mixed | P1 | banks, insurance, capital_markets, reits, foreign_filers | live |
| `cash_to_mcap` | Cash / market cap | (cash + st_investments) / market_cap (untagged short-term investments count as none).<br>**Tells you:** Cash and short-term investments as a share of market cap.<br>**Misleads when:** It ignores debt, and cash held abroad, restricted or owed to customers counts the same as free cash. | cash, st_investments, market_cap | frac | ↑ | price | mixed | P0 | foreign_filers | live |
| `goodwill_to_assets` | Goodwill + intangibles / assets | (goodwill + intangibles) / total_assets.<br>**Tells you:** Goodwill and intangibles as a share of total assets, a measure of how much of the balance sheet came from acquisitions.<br>**Misleads when:** Companies that built their brands in-house carry none, so it reflects acquisition history more than real intangible value. | goodwill, intangibles, total_assets | frac | ↓ | sec | mrq | P1 | — | live |

## Efficiency and reinvestment

| id | Name | Definition | Inputs | Unit | Better | Tier | Basis | P | n/m for | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `asset_turnover` | Asset turnover | revenue_ttm / average total_assets.<br>**Tells you:** Revenue per dollar of assets: how much selling the balance sheet supports.<br>**Misleads when:** It differs hugely by industry and rises when assets are written down, not only when the business improves. | revenue, total_assets | x | ↑ | sec | mixed | P1 | — | live |
| `dso` | Days sales outstanding | receivables (MRQ) / revenue_ttm × 365.<br>**Tells you:** Roughly how many days customers take to pay.<br>**Misleads when:** Seasonal businesses and companies that sell receivables can look unusually good or bad at one quarter end. | receivables, revenue | days | ↓ | sec | mixed | P1 | — | live |
| `dio` | Days inventory | inventory (MRQ) / cost_of_revenue_ttm × 365.<br>**Tells you:** Roughly how many days of sales sit in inventory.<br>**Misleads when:** Seasonal stock-builds before a busy period look like a warning sign when they're normal. | inventory, cost_of_revenue | days | ↓ | sec | mixed | P1 | banks, insurance, capital_markets | live |
| `dpo` | Days payables | accounts_payable (MRQ) / cost_of_revenue_ttm × 365.<br>**Tells you:** Roughly how many days the company takes to pay its suppliers.<br>**Misleads when:** A rising number can mean bargaining power or cash trouble, and the ratio can't tell which. | accounts_payable, cost_of_revenue | days | · | sec | mixed | P1 | banks, insurance, capital_markets | live |
| `cash_conversion_cycle` | Cash conversion cycle | dso + dio − dpo.<br>**Tells you:** Days of inventory plus days to collect from customers, minus days to pay suppliers: how long cash is tied up.<br>**Misleads when:** Each part is a single quarter-end snapshot, so seasonal businesses swing a lot. | dso, dio, dpo | days | ↓ | sec | mixed | P1 | banks, insurance, capital_markets | live |
| `capex_to_revenue` | Capex / revenue | capex_ttm / revenue_ttm (capex is a positive outflow in XBRL).<br>**Tells you:** Capital spending as a share of revenue: how much reinvestment the business needs.<br>**Misleads when:** It doesn't separate spending to stand still from spending to grow. | capex, revenue | frac | · | sec | ttm | P1 | — | live |
| `capex_to_dna` | Capex / D&A | capex_ttm / dna_ttm.<br>**Tells you:** Capital spending compared with depreciation: above 1 suggests the asset base is growing, below 1 that it's shrinking.<br>**Misleads when:** Acquisitions add depreciation without capex, and inflation makes replacement cost more than old depreciation. | capex, dna | x | · | sec | ttm | P1 | — | live |

## Quality and accounting

| id | Name | Definition | Inputs | Unit | Better | Tier | Basis | P | n/m for | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `piotroski_f` | Piotroski F-score | The 9 binary tests of Piotroski (2000), latest FY vs prior FY, scaled as in the paper by total assets at the start of each year: ROA > 0, CFO > 0, ΔROA > 0, CFO > NI, Δ(long-term debt / average assets) < 0, Δcurrent ratio > 0, diluted shares not up (prior count adjusted for filing-confirmed splits), Δgross margin > 0, Δasset turnover > 0. Null if any input is missing (long-term debt must be tagged). The 9 parts are stored in metric_history as piotroski_f.<test>. n/m for banks and insurers.<br>**Tells you:** A 0–9 count of nine pass/fail tests that ask whether profitability, funding and efficiency improved over the last year.<br>**Misleads when:** Every test weighs the same and only compares two years, so small changes count as much as big ones. | net_income, total_assets, cfo, debt_noncurrent, current_assets, current_liabilities, diluted_shares, gross_profit, revenue | score | ↑ | sec | fy | P0 | banks, insurance | live |
| `accruals_ratio` | Accruals ratio (Sloan-style) | (net_income_ttm − cfo_ttm) / average total_assets.<br>**Tells you:** How far reported profit ran ahead of operating cash flow, compared with the size of the balance sheet.<br>**Misleads when:** Growing companies build working capital naturally, so a high value isn't always a warning. | net_income, cfo, total_assets | frac | ↓ | sec | mixed | P0 | — | live |
| `payout_ratio` | Payout ratio | dividends_paid_ttm / net_income_ttm. Null (NEGATIVE_DENOMINATOR) if NI ≤ 0. Untagged dividends / buybacks / issuance count as none (noted) when the period's cash-flow statement is tagged (CFO present); otherwise MISSING_INPUT.<br>**Tells you:** Dividends paid as a share of the last twelve months' profit.<br>**Misleads when:** Profit includes non-cash items, so a payout that looks covered may not be covered by cash. | dividends_paid, net_income | frac | · | sec | ttm | P1 | — | live |
| `fcf_payout_ratio` | FCF payout | dividends_paid_ttm / fcf_ttm. Null (NEGATIVE_DENOMINATOR) if FCF ≤ 0. Untagged dividends / buybacks / issuance count as none (noted) when the period's cash-flow statement is tagged (CFO present); otherwise MISSING_INPUT.<br>**Tells you:** Dividends paid as a share of the last twelve months' free cash flow.<br>**Misleads when:** Free cash flow is lumpy, so one weak year can make a safe dividend look stretched. | dividends_paid, fcf | frac | ↓ | sec | ttm | P0 | — | live |
| `dps_no_cut_5y` | No dividend cut (5y) | True if dividends per share declared never fell by more than 1% year on year across the last 5 FYs (4 comparisons). Null (INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY) with fewer than 5 FYs, or (MISSING_INPUT) if a year's value is untagged.<br>**Tells you:** Whether dividends per share avoided a cut in each of the last five fiscal years.<br>**Misleads when:** It looks backwards only, and it can't see special dividends or a cut announced after the last filing. | dps_declared | bool | ↑ | sec | fy | P0 | — | live |

## Price and momentum

| id | Name | Definition | Inputs | Unit | Better | Tier | Basis | P | n/m for | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `return_1m` | Price return (1m) | Split-adjusted close / close 21 sessions ago − 1. Price return only (excludes dividends). Null (INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY) with fewer than 21 sessions.<br>**Tells you:** How much the share price moved over the last month, before dividends.<br>**Misleads when:** One month of price movement is mostly noise. | close | frac | · | price | daily | P0 | — | live |
| `return_3m` | Price return (3m) | Split-adjusted close / close 63 sessions ago − 1. Price return only (excludes dividends). Null (INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY) with fewer than 63 sessions.<br>**Tells you:** How much the share price moved over the last three months, before dividends.<br>**Misleads when:** Short-term moves often reverse and reflect market swings more than the company. | close | frac | · | price | daily | P0 | — | live |
| `return_6m` | Price return (6m) | Split-adjusted close / close 126 sessions ago − 1. Price return only (excludes dividends). Null (INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY) with fewer than 126 sessions.<br>**Tells you:** How much the share price moved over the last six months, before dividends.<br>**Misleads when:** It leaves out dividends, so high-yield stocks look worse than they did for holders. | close | frac | · | price | daily | P0 | — | live |
| `return_12m` | Price return (12m) | Split-adjusted close / close 252 sessions ago − 1. Price return only (excludes dividends). Null (INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY) with fewer than 252 sessions.<br>**Tells you:** How much the share price moved over the last year, before dividends.<br>**Misleads when:** It leaves out dividends and says nothing about the year ahead. | close | frac | · | price | daily | P0 | — | live |
| `momentum_12_1` | 12–1 momentum | close at t−21 / close at t−252 − 1 (skips the latest month). Price return only.<br>**Tells you:** Price change over the last year, leaving out the most recent month.<br>**Misleads when:** Momentum can reverse sharply, especially around market turns. | close | frac | ↑ | price | daily | P1 | — | live |
| `pct_from_52w_high` | Off 52-week high | close / max(close over 252 sessions) − 1.<br>**Tells you:** How far the price sits below its highest close of the last year.<br>**Misleads when:** A big drop can be a change in the business, not a discount. | close | frac | · | price | daily | P0 | — | live |
| `volatility_1y` | Volatility (1y) | stdev(daily log returns over 252 sessions) × √252.<br>**Tells you:** How much the share price typically swings, annualised from the last year of daily moves.<br>**Misleads when:** Past swings don't capture rare big events, and thinly traded stocks can look calmer than they are. | close | frac | ↓ | price | daily | P1 | — | live |
